angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 22,060,647 km at 90.58 pc = 3.26 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 49637: distance 90.58 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.022), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 90.58 +/- 1.993 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 11.0209 +/- 0.1661 mas (same row, RUWE 1.80), 66.4 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 31.71 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 49637: radius 31.71 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 260.547 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.064) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 22,060,647 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4121 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 49637: effective temperature 4121 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.079) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 49637: effective temperature 4121 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.079) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 564) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
